record.investigation_summary: The Payroll batch times out every Monday morning. Logs show autoscaling-driven worker pool scale-up preceding connection exhaustion, TooManyConnections errors, and HTTP 504 gateway timeouts. Historical RCA identified the same root cause of excessive worker threads exhausting DB connections, and the problem recurred after prior corrective actions.
observed_patterns: Every Monday morning, WorkerPoolScaleUp log warnings appear minutes before ConnectionTimeout and TooManyConnections errors.
The first occurrence of the pattern followed the enabling of autoscaling for payroll batch workers (EV-017) five days prior.
Historical incidents and RCA show the same symptom pattern and root cause of connection exhaustion due to excessive worker threads.
Connection pool pressure and TooManyConnections errors indicate DB connection usage approaching or exceeding the limit.
Gateway timeout (HTTP 504) errors coincide with batch connection acquisition timeouts.

hypotheses.candidate_root_cause: Autoscaling configuration allows worker threads to exceed the PostgreSQL connection limit, causing connection exhaustion and timeouts.
reasons: Autoscaling was enabled for payroll batch workers (EV-017) before the first incident, allowing the worker pool to scale up to 96 threads.
Logs show repeated WorkerPoolScaleUp warnings (EV-003, EV-008, EV-010, EV-005, EV-015) and the pool hitting its maximum of 96 threads (EV-016) shortly before connection errors.

Connection pool pressure (EV-014) and TooManyConnections errors (EV-013) indicate that the combined worker and portal connections exceed the DB limit, leading to timeouts (EV-002, EV-004, EV-007, EV-009, EV-011) and gateway timeout (EV-012).
recommended_validation: Verify the current autoscaling configuration (min/max threads) for the payroll batch worker deployment.
Monitor the actual number of active worker threads and DB connection usage during a Monday batch run.
Test reducing the max worker threads (e.g., to 32) and observe whether connection timeouts cease.
missing_evidence: The configured max_connections value for the PostgreSQL database.
The number of database connections consumed by the portal API during peak load.
Detailed thread count metrics for the payroll batch workers over several Mondays.

record.investigation_summary: Payroll batch times out every Monday morning with HTTP 504 errors, batch SLA exceed, and database connection acquisition latency. The pattern shows WorkerPoolScaleUp warnings followed by ConnectionTimeout, TooManyConnections, and GatewayTimeout errors. An autoscaling change enabled on 2026-03-11 allows the worker pool to scale up to 96 threads, each consuming a PostgreSQL connection. Historical RCA identified excessive worker threads consuming DB connections as a prior root cause, and the problem recurred after corrective actions that capped threads at 32, suggesting the autoscaling policy overrides the cap or the DB connection limit is insufficient for the scaled workload.
observed_patterns: Every Monday morning around 06:05 UTC, WorkerPoolScaleUp warnings appear, indicating an increase in payroll worker threads.
Within minutes after the scale-up, ConnectionTimeout errors appear (EV-002, EV-004, EV-007, EV-009, EV-011).
Later in the same window, TooManyConnections (EV-013) and GatewayTimeout (EV-012) errors are observed.
WorkerPoolAtMaximum warnings show the thread pool hitting the autoscaling maximum of 96 threads (EV-016).
ConnectionPoolPressure warnings indicate high DB connection usage (e.g., 176/200 connections in use, EV-014).
The autoscaling change (EV-017) preceded the first incident and coincides with the recurrence of the scale‑up pattern.
Historical RCA EV-031 found a similar root cause: excessive batch worker threads consuming DB connections (max_connections=100).
After the RCA corrective action (capping threads at 32), the problem recurred, indicating the cap was not effective or the DB limit remained insufficient.

record.investigation_summary: Payroll batch times out every Monday morning with HTTP 504 gateway timeout, SLA breach, and database connection acquisition latency. Autoscaling of payroll batch workers was enabled before the first incident, and each incident is preceded by WorkerPoolScaleUp warnings followed by ConnectionTimeout, TooManyConnections, and high connection pool pressure errors. Historical incidents and a prior RCA show the same pattern of connection exhaustion due to excessive worker threads sharing a limited PostgreSQL connection pool.
observed_patterns: WorkerPoolScaleUp warnings (autoscaling) occur minutes before ConnectionTimeout errors in each incident.
Connection pool pressure and TooManyConnections errors indicate PostgreSQL connection exhaustion.
The pattern repeats across multiple Mondays and matches the root cause identified in a prior RCA (RCA-2025-00042).
The autoscaling change (EV-017) predates the first error, while all subsequent changes occur after the first error and thus cannot have caused it.
Both the payroll batch workers and the portal API depend on the same PostgreSQL database (CMDB EV-024).

hypotheses.candidate_root_cause: Autoscaling allows the payroll batch worker pool to exceed a safe number of concurrent threads, exhausting the shared PostgreSQL connection pool and causing timeouts.
reasons: Autoscaling was enabled before the first incident (EV-017) and each incident is preceded by WorkerPoolScaleUp warnings (EV-003, EV-005, EV-008, EV-010, EV-015).
Connection timeout and pool pressure errors follow the scaling events (EV-002, EV-004, EV-007, EV-009, EV-011, EV-012, EV-013, EV-014).
The prior RCA (EV-031) identified the same mechanism: too many worker threads consuming almost all DB connections.
recommended_validation: Check the actual number of payroll batch worker threads (or pod replicas) during a Monday batch run.
Measure PostgreSQL connection usage and compare it to the configured max_connections during the same window.
Review the autoscaling policy configuration (metrics, thresholds, min/max) to see if it can exceed a safe thread count.
missing_evidence: Real‑time thread count metrics for the batch workers during incidents.
PostgreSQL max_connections setting and observed connection usage at peak load.
Autoscaling decision logs showing why the pool scaled to the observed thread count.

why_chain.why: Why did the payroll batch gateway return HTTP 504 and the batch job exceed SLA?
why_chain.because: The application could not acquire a database connection within the timeout period.

why_chain.why: Why could the application not acquire a database connection in time?
why_chain.because: The PostgreSQL connection pool was exhausted (all connections in use).

why_chain.why: Why was the connection pool exhausted?
why_chain.because: The payroll batch worker pool had too many concurrent threads, each holding a connection.

why_chain.why: Why did the worker pool have too many concurrent threads?
why_chain.because: Autoscaling was configured to allow the pool to scale up to 96 threads without a limit tied to the database capacity.

why_chain.why: Why was the database connection limit not sufficient for the scaled worker pool?
why_chain.because: The PostgreSQL max_connections setting was not increased proportionally to accommodate the possible thread count.

reasons: Autoscaling enabled before first error (EV-017) and worker pool scaled up minutes before connection timeouts (EV-003, EV-002).

Connection timeout logs and pool pressure warnings appeared shortly after the deployment of v4.18.2 and recurred the next day after a pod restart. The Payment API pods were restarted the day before the morning peak failures, as referenced in EV-001.
Past RCA EV-013 identified unclosed SQL sessions in the payment retry handler as the root cause and applied fixes, yet the problem recurred.
A change to dashboard thresholds (EV-008) was made after the first error and thus cannot have caused it.
An emergency rollback to v4.18.1 (EV-009) was performed after the incident.

Inspect the retry handler code in v4.18.2 for missing try‑with‑resources or unclosed resources.

record.investigation_summary: Payment API experienced intermittent HTTP 500 errors, latency >5 seconds, and database connection timeouts. The first errors appeared 34 minutes after deploying Payment API v4.18.2, accompanied by connection pool pressure warnings. Similar symptoms occurred in past incidents, and a prior RCA identified unclosed SQL sessions in the retry handler as root cause. The problem recurred after a pod restart, indicating a persistent issue.
observed_patterns: Connection timeout logs (EV-002) and pool pressure warnings (EV-003) began shortly after the deployment of Payment API v4.18.2 (EV-007).
The same symptoms (HTTP 500, latency >5s, connection timeouts) appeared in historical incidents EV-012, EV-013, and EV-014.
Connection pool utilization remained high (near capacity) across both error episodes (EV-003, EV-005).
The issue persisted after a pod restart, suggesting the problem is not cleared by a simple restart.

hypotheses.candidate_root_cause: The deployment of Payment API v4.18.2 introduced a defect in the payment retry handler that leaves SQL sessions unclosed during error flows, causing connection pool exhaustion and timeouts.
reasons: The v4.18.2 deploy (EV-007) occurred 34 minutes before the first connection timeout logs (EV-002).
Connection pool pressure warnings (EV-003) show active connections near capacity concurrent with timeout errors.
A prior RCA (EV-013) identified unclosed SQL sessions in the retry handler block during error responses as the root cause for identical symptoms.
recommended_validation: Inspect the retry handler code in v4.18.2 for missing try-with-resources or close() calls on JDBC resources.
Verify HikariCP leak detection is enabled and examine any leaked connection stack traces from the incident period.
Compare connection usage metrics before and after a canary rollout of v4.18.2 to see if active connections rise abnormally.
missing_evidence: Leak detection status and detailed connection leak stack traces during EV-002/EV-004 windows.
Code diff showing whether try-with-resources blocks were added to repository query methods after the past RCA.
Database session counts (active/idle) observed from the PostgreSQL side during the incident.
